Capital markets just went agent-native.

Bloomberg launched Enterprise MCP this week — exposing licensed financial data, metadata, and semantic context to AI agents through Model Context Protocol. At the same time, Nasdaq introduced a governed agentic operating environment inside Calypso for AI execution across capital markets and treasury workflows.

The design principle both share is what makes this significant for every industry: agents need authoritative business context and permissions, not just access to more data.

Bloomberg is not opening a data pipe. It is giving agents structured understanding of what data means, how it is licensed, and what decisions it can support. Nasdaq is not bolting AI onto trading desks. It is building a governed execution layer with defined permissions.

This is the blueprint. If your agents cannot distinguish between data they can act on and data they can only observe, you have exposure — not strategy.
